text:
ryan: Heads-up: gateway forwarding raw API keys is causing scope leaks in a couple services. Need a pragmatic pattern.
nika: Agreed. Two quick options: forward key (fast) or brokered ephemeral tokens (safe+slow).
sam: Performance data: broker mint p50 ~80ms, p95 ~240ms. Fanout to 3 services serially is painful.
zoe: Alternative: gateway issues short signed assertions (signed JWT) asserting client_id + scopes + exp. Downstreams verify gateway signature.
ryan: Pros: low-latency, no broker QPS. Cons: revocation is TTL-limited and requires trust distribution.
nika: We should require assertion scopes subset(original_scopes) in gateway. Also include orig_key_id for audit.
sam: For critical routes (billing) make default strict = brokered tokens with push revoke. For others use signed assertions with 5s expiry.
zoe: Small header draft:
X-RW-Assertion: <signed-jwt>
X-RW-Orig-Key: key_123
X-RW-Req: r_abc
ryan: Migration: add verifier lib, opt-in routes, monitor assertion_verify_latency, cache_hit_rate, broker_mint_rate.
auth-bot: RFC created: https://internal.redwood/rfc/assertions-17654 - please review :thumbsup:
ryan: I'll write the RFC fragment and a minimal gateway plugin. Thanks.
